name: Mirage
desc: A landscape seen through air that will not hold a straight line — a scorching floor thins the layer above it until light skims up off nothing and lays a sheet of false water across the ground, or a cold inversion bends the rays down over the horizon and hauls distant ridges up into the towering stacked and inverted castles of a Fata Morgana; every ray is traced through the actual refractivity profile, and thermal turbulence shreds the image into shimmer.

energy.doc: thermal turbulence — how hard the shimmer shreds the image — plus exposure (master knob)

scale.doc: telephoto compression — high narrows the field of view onto the mirage layer itself

speed.doc: shimmer + thermal breathing + horizon drift rate

density.doc: depth of the anomalous layer (its scale height) and atmospheric haze

grad.doc: thermal gradient. Above ~0.35 the floor is hot and rays bend up into an inferior mirage (false water); below, the air inverts and rays bend down into a superior mirage / Fata Morgana

hue.doc: ground hue — the sky and ridge are derived from it (34 = desert ochre; try 200 for a cold flat)

y.doc: eye height above the surface — low puts you down in the mirage layer where it is strongest

style.doc: aesthetic; 'grid' shows the mechanism by refracting a blueprint reference target instead of a landscape

act.doc: multi-minute programme: 'noon' holds a hot-floor inferior mirage, 'inversion' holds a cold Fata Morgana, 'breathe' walks the gradient through zero so the mirage inverts from one to the other across sections

seed.doc: seed — the ridge/skyline profile, drift phases, sensor grain
